cards.front: Recall a key point about Physical Skills in Dance
cards.back: Physical skills are the foundation of all dance performance and underpin technical and expressive work

cards.front: Recall a key point about Physical Skills in Dance
cards.back: Flexibility is the range of movement at a joint and allows dancers to achieve extended lines and shapes

cards.front: Recall a key point about Physical Skills in Dance
cards.back: Strength is the ability of muscles to exert force and is needed for lifts, jumps and controlled movements

cards.front: Recall a key point about Physical Skills in Dance

cards.front: Recall a key point about Physical Skills in Dance
cards.back: Coordination is the ability to use different body parts together smoothly and accurately

cards.front: Recall a key point about Physical Skills in Dance
cards.back: Balance is the ability to maintain a stable position, whether static or moving through space

cards.front: Recall a key point about Physical Skills in Dance
cards.back: A dancer must develop all five physical skills together as they are interdependent

cards.front: Recall a key point about Physical Skills in Dance

cards.front: Recall a key point about Physical Skills in Dance
cards.back: Muscular strength supports control in slow movements and power in explosive actions

cards.front: Recall a key point about Physical Skills in Dance
cards.back: Stamina ensures the quality of movement does not deteriorate as the performance progresses

cards.front: Recall a key point about Physical Skills in Dance

cards.front: What should you know about gcse dance exam tips — physical skills in dance?
cards.back: 1. For Physical Skills in Dance questions, identify the relevant area of law and state the legal principles clearly 2. Apply legal rules to the facts of the scenario — don't just state the law 3. When evaluating, consider both the effectiveness and fairness of legal rules 4. Reference relevant cases and statutes when discussing Physical Skills in Dance 5. Consider reform proposals and alternative approaches where relevant
